In its most recent deal, it sold its viewing rights to domestic audiences for £6.7bn over four years, with almost as much coming from

"For 18 to 34-year-olds, it's over 70% who admit to doing this regularly," says Daniel Monaghan, a researcher at Ampere Analysis.
"Over half of 35 to 44s admit to doing it, and about a third of those aged 45 to 64."

"Getting every single game will cost you hundreds of pounds a year."

Starlink services, claiming tech firm SpaceX imposed the restrictions in response to a "message from [the] American government."
Starlink is a satellite internet network operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX to provide internet service to the U.S. and other counties. Since 2024, the U.S.
Defense Department has shared a high-powered military version of the network called Starshield with Ukraine, which has cost the Pentagon billions of dollars.
It's unclear why Ukraine has experienced restricted access to Starshield.

evidence.quote: People in the Canadian province of Alberta are voting on whether to stay in Canada or begin a process for a second, binding referendum on
By 2030, those in Québec could face a similar choice.
Alberta’s grievances focus on federal economic, energy and climate policies, immigration and political representation.
Québec’s concern is the protection of its distinctive language and culture in an anglo-dominated North America.
Trump’s tariffs have affected the two provinces differently — and they’ve responded accordingly.
Alberta is among the least affected by Trump’s tariffs because its exports of oil, gas and beef are exempted.
In May, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced a referendum with two options in a clear bid to unite her divided United Conservative Party (UCP).
The move followed a court’s dismissal of a citizen petition on independence pushed by separatist elements within the party.
Polls show that some 70 per cent of people in Alberta and Québec favour remaining in Canada, and many oppose the referendums.
Through three stints governing, the PQ has held two independence referendums.
The 1980 vote failed by 40-60 per cent of voter support, and in 1995, those wanting to separate from Canada lost by a narrow
Taylor Swift got some of the old gang back together for her first full-band performance since the Eras Tour, delivering a four-song set to a
black-tie audience Saturday night at the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala.
As an indicator of just how long she’s been off any kind of regular performance circuit, the gala-capping show included Swift’s first-ever live rendering of
“The Fate of Ophelia,” the smash hit single she released just over a year ago, on Oct. 3, 2025.
As expected, she also sang her contender for the 2027 Oscars, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the Pixar film “Toy Story 5.”
Her backing crew had some singers and players who would be familiar to Swifties, but also some differences in the lineup, which was stripped down
in some regards and packed out in others, namely with a horn section.
She was joined by two sax players — not a regular staple of her touring outfit — as well as four singers and a guitarist,
For the remaining two slots in her set, Swift dug farther back into the past, covering both her cynical and romantic bases, opening with “Blank
Space” and ending with “Love Story.”
